test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following government bodies is responsible for disaster response and management at the national level in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NDMA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** is the **apex body** responsible for disaster management in India.
 
• It was **established under the Disaster Management Act, 2005**, which provides a legal framework for disaster preparedness, mitigation, and response at the national level.
 
• The NDMA is headed by the **Prime Minister of India**, who acts as the Chairperson.
 
• Its primary role is to formulate policies, plans, and guidelines for disaster management and coordinate with various ministries, departments, and state governments for implementation.
 
• NDMA conducts **disaster risk reduction and preparedness programs**, facilitates capacity building, and ensures the availability of funds for disaster response and recovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SDRF (State Disaster Response Force):**

 
 
• SDRF is established by state governments to **handle disaster response at the state level**.
 
• It operates under the guidelines provided by NDMA but focuses on state-specific disaster management activities.
 
• It is responsible for immediate rescue and relief operations in case of disasters within the state.
 
 
 
• **IRDA (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India):**
 
 
• IRDA is a statutory body formed under the **IRDA Act, 1999**.
 
• It regulates and promotes the insurance and reinsurance industry in India.
 
• Its primary focus is on protecting policyholders' interests rather than disaster management.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• NITI Aayog, established in **2015**, is the **policy think tank of the Government of India**.
 
• Its focus is on fostering cooperative federalism and developing long-term strategies for economic growth and development.
 
• It does not directly handle disaster management but may provide strategic inputs on disaster-related policies.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Disaster Management Act, 2005:**
 
 
• The Act envisages the creation of the NDMA at the national level, along with State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) and District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs) at the state and district levels.
 
• It emphasizes a proactive approach to disaster preparedness, mitigation, and response.
 
• It mandates the creation of National Policy on Disaster Management and National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NDMA's Vision:**

 
 
• To build a safe and disaster-resilient India by developing a culture of prevention, preparedness, and mitigation.
 
• To ensure a coordinated and prompt response during disasters.
 
 
 
• **Significant Initiatives by NDMA:**
 
 
• Implementation of the **National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project** (NCRMP).
 
• Promotion of Early Warning Systems for disasters like cyclones, earthquakes, and floods.
 
• Capacity building and training programs for disaster response teams.
